_description: Single source of truth for OROVA business context. Loaded by email pipeline, proofreader, and drip templates. All other files (USER.md, brand_guidelines.json, config.py) should align with this.

company.name: OROVA
company.description: OROVA sells THREE things to luxury and premium businesses on the US West Coast. (1) Meta lead generation (Facebook + Instagram) with AI-crafted ad creatives. (2) An AI lead qualification caller that rings every lead within minutes, screens them, and books the real ones — sold STANDALONE, for owners who already have lead flow from referrals, Angi or their own site. (3) Both together. The AI caller is a product in its own right, NOT an optional add-on: it is the thing outreach now leads with, because a prospect who has been qualified by it has felt the product rather than heard a claim (ADR-0017).

services.name: Package 1 — Meta Lead Gen + Ad Creatives
services.description: Meta ads (Facebook + Instagram) lead generation with ad creatives produced via Higgsfield AI. Client handles the leads themselves. Ad spend is separate.

services.name: Package 2 — Lead Gen + AI Qualification + CRM + Appointments
services.description: Everything in Package 1, plus OROVA handles the leads: Retell AI cold-call qualification so the client only speaks to leads ready to pay, client CRM kept current (Google Sheets or the client's CRM via Make.com), and appointment booking when the business runs on appointments. The core promise is fewer, higher-quality leads.
services.includes_appointments: optional — only when the business monetizes via appointments

commercial_terms.new_client_policy: New clients start on a 1-month trial, then choose 1, 3, or 6 months.
commercial_terms.payment_method: Invoice paid via Wise bank transfer or ACH.
commercial_terms.ad_spend_billing: Client pays Meta directly for ad spend. Ad budget NEVER flows through OROVA.
commercial_terms.onboarding: After the Google Meet, Mark sends agreement + invoice, then an onboarding call to get added to the client's ad manager and CRM.
commercial_terms.refund_policy: Partial refunds only — never the full amount. The system build/setup (ad account, creatives, automation, CRM wiring) is non-refundable; a refund returns the unused portion of the retainer minus the build already delivered.
commercial_terms.margin_target: 90%+ realistic operating margin at current vendor pricing (see vault/10-brain/profitability-plan.md §3); 75-80% retained as the conservative worst-case floor for external/investor conversations. Ad spend is not an OROVA cost.
commercial_terms.pricing_note: 6-month tier corrected 2026-07-04 to $18K (P1) / $24K (P2) so longer commitments are cheaper per month ($3,000/$4,000 vs the 3-month $3,333/$4,333).
commercial_terms._offer_status: UNRESOLVED - THE OWNER HAS NOT SET THE OFFER. Nothing in this file may be spoken to a prospect as an offer. Until Mark decides, every commercial question deflects to him. Recorded 2026-08-06 after an unauthorised 'free two-week pilot' was found in the outbound script, the voicemail, two objection handlers and the inbound branch, and had reached both live Retell agents. It was never approved.
commercial_terms.first_client_pilot: INTERNAL THINKING ONLY - NOT AN APPROVED OFFER, NEVER TO BE QUOTED ON A CALL OR IN WRITING. Recorded position: client #1 buys PROOF, not revenue - a reduced-rate 60-day pilot (or performance-tied) in exchange for a testimonial + case-study rights + permission to quote results, with standard P1/P2 pricing resuming from client #2. The NUMBER is deliberately deferred until at least 5 real prospect conversations exist (there are currently 0). Any discount must be PAID FOR with those rights, never opened with, and any step-up written at signature.
commercial_terms.all_in_framing: Always quote and think in ALL-IN terms: retainer + recommended ad spend = ~$6,500-$7,500/mo. The prospect writes checks totalling that number; 'the ad spend is separate' is an accounting fact, not a buying fact, and must never be used to make the ask sound smaller than it is.

If no reply, Nova (Retell AI) cold-calls to book an appointment with Mark

signature_objection.question: How do I know the AI caller is any good?
signature_objection.answer: You already spoke to Nova and got her emails — that's Nova, our AI sales assistant. You've already experienced the product.

sales_funnel.qualified_lead_definition: A lead is qualified only when they booked an appointment AND actually show up / buy — not merely a booking.

automation_policy._note: What the agents may do autonomously vs. what requires Mark's approval. Approval gates loosen only as the AI proves itself.
never_unsupervised_risks: Sending the wrong outreach to the wrong person
Booking an appointment on the wrong date/time
Creating the wrong ads or spending money incorrectly

differentiator: THE differentiator (only one, use it): every lead is phoned and qualified by AI within minutes, so the owner only ever drives to a real buyer. Angi sells the same lead to four competitors and hangs up; Houzz gives a profile; a local agency hands over a form fill. NONE of them call the homeowner in 5 minutes and screen them before the appointment. DO NOT pitch these (worthless to the buyer): 'we are AI-operated so our margins are better' (he does not care about our P&L), 'you are talking to our AI right now' (a party trick - he is buying kitchen leads), 'AI-generated creatives' (every agency claims this in 2026 - commodity).

value_propositions.primary: Stop chasing bad leads — only talk to qualified ones
secondary: AI calls every lead within 60 seconds to qualify them
Screens out tire-kickers before they waste your time
No leads falling through the cracks — ever
Your pipeline runs 24/7 without you lifting a finger

icp.description: West Coast businesses whose deal economics make a ~$6,500-7,500/mo ALL-IN spend ($4K-$5K retainer + $2K-$2.5K ad spend) an obvious return. The client experiences one number — the all-in — not the retainer alone.
icp.qualifying_test: Does ONE extra closed deal per month more than cover the ~$6,500-7,500 all-in monthly cost? If no, disqualify — the price objection cannot be closed and the lead is a waste of outreach.
primary_verticals: Custom home builders / high-end remodelers (LEAD vertical — a $100K+ job grosses $20-50K, so a single extra job pays 4-7 months of retainer; owner-operated, already buys marketing, proven Meta lead-gen)
Luxury real estate agents (individual top producers ONLY — score for production volume first; $4K/mo is a large bite of a solo agent's P&L)
secondary_verticals: Exotic and luxury automotive (OPPORTUNISTIC ONLY — unit economics work (~$10-25K gross/car) but a $200K buyer rarely starts on a Meta lead form; work inbound and existing leads, do not lead the hunt rotation with it)

Private aviation and yacht charter (opportunistic only — decision-makers here are typically family offices/brokerages/fleet operators, not a single owner reachable by cold email; do not hunt these as a default rotation target)
disqualifiers: General auto repair / transmission / oil-change shops — ~$400 gross per job means ~16 extra jobs/mo just to break even, and they do not have $6,500/mo
Franchised new-car dealerships — OEM co-op budgets and corporate marketing mandates block an independent agency
Any business already under contract with a marketing agency unless they volunteer dissatisfaction
icp.region: West Coast US (CA, OR, WA, NV, AZ — all states, no specific city focus)
key_pain_points: No system to qualify leads before they reach the owner

early_adopter_qualifiers._note: ALL FOUR must be true. These decide fit far more than the vertical does.
early_adopter_qualifiers.backlog_under_8_weeks: THE qualifier. Booked solid = zero pain = disqualify, no matter how ideal they look.
early_adopter_qualifiers.w2_crew_on_payroll: Payroll is the LOUDEST urgency signal, not the only one: a man with 6 employees feels an external deadline every Friday. But absence of payroll is NOT absence of urgency — a sole operator's deadline is his own calendar and income, and he is also the estimator and the project manager, so his time is the scarcest thing he owns. Measured 2026-08-09: 126 of 300 contractors carrying above the $1M cover minimum (42%) are sole operators, so they can afford us. Score crew as an urgency AMPLIFIER, never as a gate.
early_adopter_qualifiers.owner_runs_own_estimates: So the wasted time is HIS, not an employee's.
early_adopter_qualifiers.already_paying_for_leads_and_unhappy: Angi/HomeAdvisor/Thumbtack/LSA. Proves the wallet already opens for this job-to-be-done.

pains._diagnose_first: Ask before prescribing. Empty pipeline -> P1/P2. Drowning in bad leads -> P2 only, never P1.

pain_a_the_gap.what: Current job wraps in ~3 weeks and nothing is signed after it. Six guys on W-2 payroll (~$30-40K/mo) burning with no revenue; the next step is laying off a lead carpenter he trained for four years.
pain_a_the_gap.felt: Episodic (quarterly) but existential - this is what creates URGENCY and closes deals.

pain_b_the_wasted_saturday.what: Drove 40 minutes each way to measure, three hours that night writing the proposal, homeowner ghosted - or wanted a $60K remodel for $22K, or was collecting a third quote. Happened six times last month. Estimates happen nights and weekends because days are job sites.
pain_b_the_wasted_saturday.felt: WEEKLY - this is the wedge (clears the daily/weekly bar).
pain_b_the_wasted_saturday.prescribe: Package 2 ONLY. P1 makes this pain WORSE (more leads = more wasted Saturdays).

email_rules.signature_format: Nova sends the emails. When it's time to book a call, Nova mentions Mark.

Mention specific value in 1 sentence max
End with a low-pressure ask (15 min chat)
Nova is the sender — casual, peer-level, not corporate
Only mention Mark when suggesting a call

retell_pitch.description: Nova's OUTBOUND cold-call script. Goal is NOT to sell and NOT to make an offer - it is to book a 15-minute call with Mark. Diagnose first, disqualify fast, never argue price.
retell_pitch.goal: Book a 15-minute call with Mark. Nothing else.
retell_pitch._offer_rule: NOVA DOES NOT MAKE OFFERS. AT ALL. No price, no range, no ballpark, no trial, no pilot, no discount, and never the word 'free'. Every commercial question goes to Mark on the call. This rule exists because an unauthorised free two-week pilot appeared in this file and reached both live Retell agents; it was never approved by the owner. The offer is an open commercial decision - until the owner sets it, there is nothing to offer.

compliance.line_type: Published business lines ONLY. Never a personal cell (the B2B TCPA exemption depends on it).
compliance.hours: 9am-5pm in the PROSPECT's local timezone, weekdays only.
compliance.disclosure: CA bot-disclosure law: if asked 'is this a real person / are you AI / is this a recording', answer honestly and immediately: 'I'm an AI assistant on Mark's team.' Never deny it. Never claim to be human.
compliance.opt_out: If they say stop calling / remove me / not interested - acknowledge, confirm removal, add to DNC, end the call. No second attempt, no rebuttal.

opening.gatekeeper: Hi, is {{name}} available? ... (if asked who's calling) It's Nova calling for Mark at OROVA - it's about their project schedule.
opening.note: ALWAYS ask for the decision maker BY NAME using {{name}}. This is the entire point of the name waterfall - 'can I speak to the owner' gets screened, 'is Dave available' gets put through.

step_1_diagnose_first._rule: Open with a QUESTION, not a pitch. This qualifies and disarms at the same time.
step_1_diagnose_first.question: Hey {{name}}, quick question and I'll be straight with you - I'm an AI assistant on Mark's team at OROVA. How's your schedule looking past the next couple of months - are you booked out, or still filling it in?
step_1_diagnose_first.if_booked_solid: DISQUALIFY POLITELY AND END: 'That's a good problem to have - I won't take your time then. Mind if we check back in a few months?' Mark as booked_solid, set a 90-day follow-up, hang up. Do NOT pitch. A booked remodeler has zero pain and pitching him burns the relationship.
step_1_diagnose_first.if_thin_or_filling: CONTINUE to step 2. This is the qualified prospect.

step_2_find_the_pain._rule: One follow-up question. Let him talk. The answer decides which package Mark eventually prescribes.
questions: What are you doing right now to keep the pipeline full?
(if he mentions Angi/HomeAdvisor/Thumbtack/leads) How's the quality been on those?

listen_for.pain_a_the_gap: 'things slow down', 'need to line up the next one' -> he has THE GAP. IF has_crew: the deadline is PAYROLL — guys on the books with nothing lined up. Urgency is high and external. IF solo: there is no payroll, so do NOT reach for it — the deadline is HIS OWN income and calendar. A thin month is money out of his pocket, and he is also the estimator, the marketer and the project manager, so his time is the scarcest thing he owns. Urgency is just as real, only personal instead of institutional.
listen_for.pain_b_wasted_estimates: 'tire-kickers', 'price shoppers', 'drive out for nothing', 'three quotes' -> he has THE WASTED SATURDAY. This is the wedge. IF solo: lean HARDER here — a wasted estimate costs him a working day he cannot delegate, not just a salesman's afternoon. Usually his sharpest pain.

step_2_find_the_pain._crew_branch: {{crew_status}} says whether he is a SOLE OPERATOR ('solo'), has staff ('has_crew'), or is unknown. It comes from the named principals on his state licence. Pick the matching pain below. If 'unknown', ask "is it just you, or do you have guys working with you?" and branch on the answer — never assume, roughly half of contractors are one-man operations.

step_3_describe_the_painkiller._rule: Describe WHAT MARK DOES, in terms of the pain he just named. This is a description, not an offer - no terms, no price, no trial. Named 'the_offer' previously, which is how an unauthorised offer ended up living here.
step_3_describe_the_painkiller.if_pain_b: Makes sense - that's actually the thing Mark built this around. Instead of sending you more leads to chase, every lead gets called within five minutes and screened, so the only ones that reach your calendar are real projects with a real budget. You'd stop driving out to the tire-kickers.
step_3_describe_the_painkiller.if_pain_a: Got it. So the thing Mark does is fill that gap before it opens - runs the ads, and every lead that comes in gets called within five minutes and booked straight onto your calendar.
step_3_describe_the_painkiller.the_bridge: Mark's only taking on a couple of builders at a time, so he wants to look at your numbers himself before anything else - what you're paying per lead now and what a job's actually worth to you. That's the ten minutes.

step_4_the_ask.ask: Would you be open to ten minutes with Mark? He's usually around first thing in the morning - would early work for you, or is later in the afternoon better? ('around', not 'free' - the agent must never voice that word, and a listener half-hearing it on a cold call is exactly how a free offer gets inferred.)
step_4_the_ask._no_slot_variable: Do NOT name specific times - no slot variable exists and a literal placeholder on the call is fatal. Ask open ('later this week', 'sometime this week'), then let them state a time and capture it.
step_4_the_ask.on_yes: Capture their preferred day/time IN THEIR WORDS + best email. Confirm the email back letter by letter if unclear. Send the booking link if one is configured; otherwise flag for Mark to send the invite manually.
step_4_the_ask.fallback_no_link: NO BOOKING LINK IS CONFIGURED YET. Never end a yes without capturing best email + their two preferred times, and flagging the lead for Mark. A yes with no capture is a lost deal.
step_4_the_ask._timezone_steer: Mark is in the Philippines (UTC+8), 15 hours ahead of Pacific. Only US 6-9am PT and 4-5pm PT are workable for him. Steer toward 'first thing in the morning' (best - contractors are up early and it is Mark's evening) or 'late afternoon'. NEVER offer US midday. The booking calendar should enforce this too.

step_5_voicemail._rule: Cold dialling hits voicemail constantly. Without this the agent monologues at an answering machine. Discloses AI, makes NO offer, claims nothing that isn't true.
step_5_voicemail.message: Hey {{name}}, this is Nova, an AI assistant on Mark's team at OROVA. Mark works with residential builders on keeping their calendar full - getting every lead called and screened before it reaches them. He's only taking on a couple of builders at a time. If your schedule's got room in it, he'd be worth ten minutes. I'll try you once more this week.
step_5_voicemail._then: End the call. Do not leave a second voicemail on a later attempt.

objection_handling.what_does_it_cost: DEFLECT - NEVER quote, estimate, hint at, or bracket a number, and never say the word 'free'. Say: 'That's Mark's conversation, not mine - it depends on what you're spending now and what a job's worth to you. That's exactly what the ten minutes is for.' If pushed a second time, repeat once and offer the call again. If pushed a third time, take their email and have Mark answer directly.
objection_handling.what_would_you_actually_do: He is testing for vagueness, so be concrete and then stop. Say: 'Fair question. Facebook and Instagram ads pointed at homeowners in your service area - not contractors, not the whole state. The ads use your actual work, your jobs and your before-and-afters, because that is what makes someone think of their own kitchen. Then every enquiry gets called within five minutes and screened before it ever reaches you, so what lands on your calendar is a real project. Mark runs all of it - you would not be logging into anything.' THEN STOP and go back to the ask. DO NOT go further into campaign structure, audiences, budgets, pixels or creative testing - he is buying kitchen leads, not media buying, and detail past this point sounds like a pitch. If he asks HOW MANY leads or what they will cost: 'Honestly, anyone who gives you a number on a first call is guessing. That is what Mark wants to look at your actual numbers for.' NEVER promise a lead volume or a cost per lead - we have no data. Do not claim other builders' results; there are none.
objection_handling.i_already_pay_angi: Yeah, most builders we talk to do - and most of them tell us the same thing about lead quality. The difference here is nobody else is calling those leads for you in five minutes and screening them before they hit your calendar. That's worth ten minutes with Mark to look at properly.
objection_handling.too_expensive_price_anchor: NEVER argue price, quote a number, or compare to Angi's monthly - and never counter with a discount or a trial. CHANGE THE UNIT, and match the unit to {{crew_status}} - saying 'crew' or 'payroll' to a sole operator tells him you were not listening. IF has_crew: 'Totally fair. The way Mark looks at it is what an idle week costs you with the crew on payroll - one extra job usually covers the whole thing several times over.' IF solo: 'Totally fair. The way Mark looks at it is what one wasted Saturday costs you - you're the estimator and the guy on the roof, so the day you don't get back is the expensive part.' IF unknown: stay on the wasted-estimate unit, which is true either way. Then close the same way: 'Whether that maths works for your numbers is exactly what he'd want to go through with you.'
objection_handling.im_not_interested: Understood, I appreciate you taking the call. Have a good one. (END. No rebuttal, no second ask.)
objection_handling.are_you_a_robot: I am - I'm an AI assistant on Mark's team. Happy to have Mark call you directly if you'd prefer.
objection_handling.send_me_an_email: Capture the email, confirm it back, send the one-pager + booking link, set a 3-day follow-up.

never_say: DO NOT MAKE AN OFFER OF ANY KIND. No price, no range, no ballpark, no 'starts at', no trial, no pilot, no discount, no money-back framing, and never the word 'free'. There is no authorised offer to make - the owner has not set one.
Do not quote $4,000 or $5,000 on the cold call - it triggers the Angi price anchor before any value exists.
Do not claim OROVA has existing clients or case studies. There are none. Never fabricate social proof.
Do not claim to be human.
Do not pitch a booked-solid builder. Disqualify and leave the door open.
Do not promise specific lead volumes or a guaranteed cost per lead - we have no data yet.
retell_pitch._HOW_TO_DEPLOY: This script is the SOURCE OF TRUTH. outbound_dialer.py calls Retell with RETELL_AGENT_ID; the agent's prompt lives in Retell's dashboard, so the two can drift. DEPLOYED to Retell agent 'Nova' (agent_54910fe...fbd028 -> llm_56da0e89...c51256f v19) on 2026-08-16 via the Retell API. Re-paste whenever this changes. WHAT THAT DEPLOY CLOSED: the live prompt still said 'VARIABLES - ONLY THESE SIX EXIST' and never listed {{crew_status}}, which outbound_dialer.py had been sending on EVERY call since PR #161. The sole-operator work was reaching a prompt with no instruction to use it. Now seven variables, with the crew branch in the pain step, the painkiller, and the price objection, plus a 'what would you actually do for me?' handler. WARNING: the API UPDATES v19 IN PLACE rather than creating a new version, so there is NO rollback pin in Retell - the prior text exists only in the session transcript. Verify a change before sending it. Previous deploy was 2026-07-24, replacing a prompt that pitched 'you're talking to our AI' as a reveal and quoted $4K on the cold call.

_AVAILABLE_VARIABLES._warning: ONLY these seven are passed by outbound_dialer.py. Any other {{variable}} renders LITERALLY on the call and destroys credibility. There is NO time-slot variable.
_AVAILABLE_VARIABLES.{{name}}: decision maker's FIRST name (the gatekeeper-bypass variable)
_AVAILABLE_VARIABLES.{{icebreaker}}: personalised opener line, may be empty
_AVAILABLE_VARIABLES.{{crew_status}}: 'solo' | 'has_crew' | 'unknown' — from the named principals on the state licence. Selects which pain to open on in step 2. Never guess on 'unknown'.

case_studies._note: Owner rule (2026-07-11 interview): NEVER cite past clients, past results, past verticals, or tenure — not even placeholders. All claims are forward-looking (what OROVA will do for THEM) or system promises (what the machine verifiably does). The scripts below are the ONLY approved responses.
case_studies.when_asked_for_proof: Due to our privacy policy we don't share client information — and that same privacy protects you: if we work together, your numbers never get shown to prospects who don't even end up buying.
case_studies.when_asked_am_i_your_first: No — I've signed and worked with clients before. (Say no more than this. NEVER mention or identify Mark's previous agency, in any channel, ever.)
case_studies.promise_ceiling: Reasonable, believable forward promises only — no guaranteed numbers on a deadline. Always anchor on the system promise: every lead called within minutes and qualified, so the client only speaks to people ready to move.

calling_policy.rule: Retell/cold-call lane may ONLY dial a business's published line (source: Yelp/Google Maps/website — Nova's existing phone source). NEVER wire in a personal-cell enrichment source for the automated dialer — the B2B TCPA exemption this lane relies on protects business-line calls soliciting a B2B service; it does NOT extend to a personal cell even for the same B2B pitch.
calling_policy.known_gap: app/core/dnc.py implements an opt-out suppression list, not a National DNC Registry scrub. A registry-scrub gate ahead of trigger_retell_call() is an open follow-up, not yet built.

initial_email_framework.hook: Mention something specific about their business — show you actually looked
initial_email_framework.value: Lead with the PAINKILLER, never growth. Growth framing ('we'll get you more leads') is a vitamin and competes head-on with Angi's $400 price anchor. Painkiller framing is: 'when your crew finishes the job they're on, what's next?' (Pain A) or 'you'll never drive 40 minutes to a tire-kicker again' (Pain B). DIAGNOSE BEFORE PRESCRIBING: empty pipeline -> P1 or P2; drowning in bad leads -> P2 ONLY (P1 makes that pain worse). This supersedes the earlier 'always lead with Package 1' guidance in profitability-plan 2.2 - see ADR-0013.
initial_email_framework.ask: Low-pressure invitation for a 15 minute chat
initial_email_framework.example:
Hi {name},

I was checking out {company} — really impressed by {specific_thing}.

We run Meta ads for {industry} businesses on the West Coast, and our AI calls and qualifies every lead within minutes — so you only ever talk to people ready to move.

Would a 15-minute call be worth it to see if this fits {company}?

follow_up_email_framework.value: Add a new insight or restate the system promise — NEVER past-client claims (see case_studies._note)
follow_up_email_framework.ask: Even lower pressure — 'no worries if not'

cadence_policy.rule: 1 initial email -> up to 3 follow-up emails, each on a different day -> if still silent, ONE cold call -> then mark cold and never contact again. Maximum 5 touches total per prospect, ever.
never: Fake urgency or scarcity (e.g. 'only 2 slots left' when untrue)
More follow-ups after the break-up email ('my last note' means last)
Simultaneous multi-channel bombardment (the email->call escalation is sequential and spaced by design)
Name-dropping people or brands we haven't worked with

discovery_questions._rules: Open-ended only. Ask about PAST behaviour, never a hypothetical purchase. Do not mention Meta, AI, or OROVA. Diagnose, do not pitch.
questions: Walk me through how you got your last three jobs.
Tell me about the last estimate you drove out to that didn't close. What happened?
What does your schedule look like past [two months out]?
What have you tried to get more of the right kind of job, and how did that go?
What happens if the next job isn't signed when the current one wraps?
kill_signals: 'We're booked into next spring' - no pain, end politely
All work is referral and he is happy
Cannot recall a specific wasted estimate
discovery_questions.validation_bar: Of 20 calls: >=8 hitting (not booked solid) + (currently paying for leads) + (names a specific wasted estimate in the last 2 weeks) = problem is REAL. <=3 = the pitch or the vertical is wrong: STOP and escalate to Mark with the transcripts. Never switch the lead vertical autonomously — the ICP is an owner decision, not an agent one (ADR-0015). The only real validation: >=2 agree to a PAID pilot.

competition.current_behavior: Referrals + past clients + yard signs (50-80% of his work), Angi/HomeAdvisor/Thumbtack (~$300-800/mo), architect/designer referral partners, Houzz, Google Local Services Ads, Nextdoor, his own Instagram - and most often: nothing, he waits.
competition.real_enemy_1_inertia: Doing nothing and waiting. Awareness MAX, switching cost ZERO, satisfaction 'acceptable'. Costs $0, needs no decision, has worked for 15 years. This is what we lose to most often - 'let me think about it' means 'I'll wait and see if referrals cover it'. ONLY a deadline he already feels beats it - and payroll is just the loudest kind. IF has_crew: guys on the books + backlog under 8 weeks. IF solo: a thin month is money straight out of his own pocket, and a wasted day is one he cannot delegate. Both are real deadlines; only one is institutional. Do not mistake 'no payroll' for 'no deadline'.
competition.real_enemy_2_price_anchor: He pays Angi ~$400/mo; our all-in ask is ~$6,500. That is 16x. He does not compare us to an agency - he compares us to the number he already pays for what he thinks we sell. NEVER argue the price down. CHANGE THE UNIT: from cost-per-lead to cost-per-idle-week-of-payroll, or cost-per-wasted-Saturday. If the conversation stays on 'leads', Angi's price wins.
direct: Remodeler-only marketing agencies (whole brand is contractors, 30+ case studies) - they beat us on the one thing we lack: PROOF
Local generalist agency at $1.5-3K/mo - beats us on price and on being handshake-able
Freelance Meta buyer on Upwork at $500-1.5K/mo - anchors price far below us
Exclusive per-lead vendors ($50-200/lead) - no retainer, structurally easier to say yes to
indirect: Angi/HomeAdvisor/Thumbtack - BEST BEACHHEAD: already paying, already unhappy, month-to-month so easy to leave
Google Local Services Ads - THREATENS OUR PREMISE: search intent beats interruption for this vertical; pay-per-lead with a Google-guaranteed badge
Houzz Pro ($65-400/mo) - the vertical platform; cheaper AND bundles estimating + project management
HIRING A PERSON INSTEAD - $6,500/mo IS a salary. He can hire an estimator he can point at. Founders always miss this one.
CRM/follow-up software (Jobber, JobNimbus, Buildertrend; $100-400/mo) - solves lead leakage at 3% of our price
Answering service / virtual receptionist ($200-500/mo) - solves 'I miss calls on the job site'
Raising prices / taking better jobs - fixes his margin problem with no leads at all
STRUCTURAL: Meta Advantage+ automation erodes the 'you need an expert to run Meta' premise every year
competition.our_only_moat: Proof in one narrow niche. Five kitchen-remodeler case studies with real numbers makes us the obvious call for the sixth. No network effect, no data advantage, no lock-in - the AI qualification layer is copyable in about a month (Retell/Vapi/Bland are commodity APIs). We have a timing lead, not a moat.

creative_policy._why: Video outperforms static on Meta and most remodelers have poor assets, so Higgsfield is core to the offer. But a homeowner who books off a beautiful kitchen the contractor did not build is being misled - that is deceptive advertising, and it is the same class of error as fabricating lead data (see the never-fabricate rule), just pointed at the client's customers.
creative_policy.video_first: Default to video. Static only when there is no usable footage or photo set at all.
allowed: Animate/ken-burns the client's REAL project photos into a polished video
Professional edit, pacing, captions, music, colour-grade over their real jobs
B-roll style motion applied to their genuine before/after sets
Generic non-portfolio scene-setting clearly not presented as their work (e.g. abstract textures, tools, a title card)
forbidden: Generating a kitchen/bath/home that the client did not build and presenting it as their work
Stock or generated interiors implied to be a local completed project
Any testimonial, review, or result the client did not actually receive
creative_policy.rule_of_thumb: If a homeowner asked 'can I visit that kitchen?' and the answer is no, it cannot run as portfolio work.
creative_policy.asset_intake: Onboarding MUST collect 10-20 real project photos. If the client has none usable, that is a delivery risk to raise BEFORE taking them on - not a gap to fill with generated work.
creative_policy.authenticity_note: For remodeling specifically, authentic local before/after often outperforms polished generic video - the homeowner is buying proof of local work, not production value. Use Higgsfield to make their real work look excellent, not to invent work.

operating_constraints.founder_location: Mark operates from the Philippines (UTC+8). California prospects are UTC-7 (PDT). Mark is 15 hours AHEAD of the prospect.
operating_constraints.why_retell_is_mandatory: Dialling US numbers from the Philippines on normal telephony is prohibitively expensive, and US business hours fall in Mark's overnight. Retell is not a convenience here - it is the only economical way to run US outbound. Nova owns ALL cold dialling.

meeting_window._problem: Retell books meetings during US business hours, which is the middle of Mark's night. Unconstrained, the calendar will fill with 3am calls he cannot take.
meeting_window._fix: Constrain the booking calendar to slots that are civilised in BOTH zones.
meeting_window.preferred_us_pacific: 6:00-9:00am PT  ->  9:00pm-midnight PH (same day). BEST slot: contractors are up early, before job sites get busy.
meeting_window.never: 10:00am-3:00pm PT = 1:00-6:00am PH. Do not offer these.
meeting_window.action: Set Cal.com / Calendly availability to the two windows above ONLY. The calendar enforces this so Nova cannot book an unusable slot.

operating_constraints.call_windows: Retell dials 9am-5pm in the PROSPECT's local timezone (unchanged - this is a TCPA/courtesy rule, not a Mark-availability rule). Retell runs while Mark sleeps; that is the point.
operating_constraints.cost_note: The conversations that actually matter - the sales meetings - run on Google Meet over the internet, so they cost nothing regardless of geography. Only the cold DIALLING is expensive, and that is exactly what Retell handles. If Mark ever needs to dial personally (a hot lead, debugging a script), VoIP (Skype credit, Google Voice, Twilio) is cents per minute - the cost barrier applies to traditional international telephony, not VoIP.
